verdict.tagline: A brilliant cooperative adventure that stumbles slightly on forced split-screen.
for_you_if: you want a game built entirely around genuine cooperation
you enjoy a stream of fresh puzzles and mechanics
you have a dedicated partner for the journey
not_for_you_if: you cannot stand forced split-screen presentation
you require stable online connections without lag
you need achievements while using the guest pass
you are sensitive to flashing visual sequences

distortion_flags.sentence: Approval climbs steeply as players move past initial split-screen friction and technical hurdles.

cohorts.summary: Players discover fresh mechanics and praise the cooperative puzzle design despite a grim narrative beat.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay as continuously introducing fresh and varied mechanics, puzzles, and minigames across different chapters.

citations.review_text: This game is undoubtedly Game of the Year deserved. Every section and little detail in the game is masterful and every single puzzle is co-op perfection. The minigames and story add to the already great experience making this a masterpiece video game.

Played this with my duo and honestly this game will test both your teamwork and your patience. 😂 We laughed a lot, argued a lot, blamed each other for dying, then somehow continued playing like nothing happened.

I love how the game keeps introducing new mechanics and environments, so it never really gets boring. Every chapter feels different and there are so many random little things you can interact with. The story was also surprisingly emotional underneath all the chaos.

Definitely one of the best co-op games I've played. Just make sure you play it with someone you won't unfriend halfway through. 😭

10/10. Would argue with my duo again.

This is the best Co-op game I've ever played in my life. If you got a good friend and are looking for fun co-op games to play, this is your best bet. Every chapter, every level is something new. The game not only looks good with its graphics but also has new mechanics and different ways of solving puzzles so it doesn't get stale so often as you keep playing, you literally never know what will happen next. With that being said, you must work together very well and that's what this game does best, the co-op experience. You rely alot on each other to get past certain areas and mobs and that communication really drew me and my friend to work well together. The story being tied into the game mechanics and the levels all in all make this game amazing. I haven't even finished it yet but god, it's so good. Highly recommend!

Very fun, very pretty graphics, and a good several hours of content to play with a buddy. Would highly recommend. 

Also I love Dr. Hakim lmaooo

If I had to describe this game in one word it would be: Magnificent.

Now I finally understand how a co-op game won 2021 GOTY. I knew It Takes Two was highly praised but I never expected it to be this freaking good.

The game feels much bigger and more ambitious than Hazelight's previous title "A Way Out". It's a wholesome and heartfelt story about a family falling apart and finding a way back together. May and Cody's journey is very emotional and surprisingly relatable.

What impressed me the most was how every chapter introduced fresh mechanics and gameplay ideas. Just when you think you've seen everything the game has to offer, it throws something completely new at you. You can actually feel the amout of work the devs have putten into it.

The visuals are gorgeous, the levels are fun to explore and the gameplay never gets repetitive. What else do you need in a game. Besides its damn cheap during Steam sales.

Overall, this is easily one of the best games I've ever played. An absolute 10/10 for me.

Great gameplay. Abhorrent story and characters.
Played through the story once, and did not want to replay it. The gameplay in the game is very enjoyable (pretty much all of it) and constantly varies to offer a new experience. But I was completely turned off by the story and its characters.
The characters are one dimensional and quite unlikable. They constantly bicker with eachother (not even argueing, just bickering) about everything and anything. Their dicision making is fully ego-centric and at times deeply disturbing. The story can at parts best be described as psychological horror. Since you cannot make any dicisions in this game, you have to play out the abhorrent story or turn the game off.

The game itself is fun to play. But the story itself is so terrible that I cannot in good conscience recommend it.
If however you ignore the story completely the game itself it very playable! So that is what I'm doing for my second playthrough. Swap the spoken language to Japanese (or any other language you are not proficient in), disable the subtitles, and skip all the cut-scenes. This way you can make your own story and make up reasons why the characters do what they do. Way more fun to play this way!

citations.review_text: was fun up until the point where you have to brutally rip a cute baby elephant limb from limb and kill it while it begs for mercy

You guys NEED to remove that elephant section. Also the main characters might be the DUMBEST people on planet earth.

They need to make their kid happy, so what do they do? 

Whatever wholesome thoughts you just had, throw them out the window because the answer was to brutally rip apart her favorite toy limb by limb. The animal is still alive and screaming throughout all of this by the way. This is when I stopped playing the game. 

Can you guess how this worked out? Poorly. Who would've thought. The situation became worse because it turns out destroying a child's favorite toy doesn't make them very happy.

An absolute blast to play. The puzzles and gameplay really depend on the cooperation and communication with your partner and were a great bonding experience. The story was very cozy and "Disney-esque" but there are some parts in the story that will leave you speechless... iykyk. Great for long distance partners via online play and probably better in couch co-op. Strongly recommended!

[b]It Takes Two[/b] is hands down the best co-op game ever made!

The concept is as simple as it is genius: two parents on the verge of divorce, with one daughter, get turned into small "puppets" inside their own home. They want to get back into their real bodies as well as to their beloved daugher. The only way? They have to work together. Both get unique tools to solve unique puzzles across unique locations in their home, and only their cooperation - despite their crumbling relationship - will bring them back.

Nothing new, right?

Weeeeell, the gameplay is absolutely unique and incredible. Preferably played with controllers, both players share a split-screen experience (locally as well as online), so each player is always visible to the other.

The key to success is good communication, similar to [b]We Were Here[/b]. But the gameplay is also extremely fun thanks to mini-games hidden throughout the levels, as well as maaaany feel-good moments, funny scenes, and constant genre shifts enabled by the tools.

For example, on your journey you'll turn into sorcerers and for a few minutes the game suddenly becomes a rogue-like RPG. Later on, the game turns into a 2D platformer like Super Mario. Then, at one point, the mother gets a scythe and suddenly you're playing a beat-'em-up! I can't stress enough how diverse this game is!

The art direction is perfect and the world design is pure bliss with much love for details!

The game is perfect for couples but also great for good friends; just be prepared for a few frustrating as well as hilarious moments!

One of the best parts? Only one of you needs to own the game! Your partner just has to download the free "Play It Takes Two – Friend's Pass" and you can jump right in.

So, jump into it and save your relationship!
[u]9/10[/u]

also my friend is the one who actually owns the game and i used the friend pass thing and that was an awesome feature
such a fun game to play with my boyfriend!! I use the friend pass and it is awesome! I love the team building and mini games along the way!

My girlfriend and I played through the entire story together, and we both absolutely loved every second of it. If you’re looking for a game to play with your partner, stop searching and just buy this.

The game never gets repetitive because every new chapter introduces completely fresh mechanics and clever puzzles. You truly have to rely on each other to progress, making every success feel like a shared victory. Plus, the world is full of fun interactive minigames, and only one person needs to own the game for both of you to play.

Whether your partner is an experienced gamer or totally new to games, It Takes Two is an unforgettable ride. Perfect date night material!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that only one player needs to own the full game while the second player can join using a limited version or friend pass.

citations.review_text: Objectively the greatest co-op game ever created. Such an incomprehensible amount of work and creativity went into this game, and it's so cheap and only 1 person needs to own it for two people to play together. I played the whole game twice through with two different friends. Highly recommended, just don't be disappointed if you don't find another co-op game like this one when you're done

A super imaginative game that encourages exploring. Aside from hidden mini-games, there are all kinds of interactive spots mixed in as well that let you just play around. It was a unique experience and I was impressed by the amount of content. There was more to it than I originally had guessed. Each area was creative and kept things fresh with a decent amount of challenge. It was great that only one person needs a full copy of the game and another can use a limited version that allows you to play along (or play locally). Totally worth playing and I will definitely check out their other games as well.

It Takes Two is one of those games I will always recommend.

The environment design is beautiful, the soundtrack is memorable, and the story is genuinely well written. I finished it with my best friend, and there were several moments that absolutely got us emotional, which says a lot about how strong the writing and character work are.

I also really appreciate co-op games that offer a Friend’s Pass. Being able to play through the whole game with someone without requiring both people to buy a copy makes it so much easier to share the experience, and It Takes Two either helped popularize that feature or is at least one of the best-known examples of it.

One important note: my friend has epilepsy, and there were parts of the game that made us feel this may not be the safest choice for players with photosensitivity or seizure concerns. If that applies to you, I would recommend proceeding with a lot of caution or possibly avoiding it.

Overall, this is a beautiful, creative, emotional co-op experience, and I think everyone who can safely play it should give it a try.

citations.review_text:
In general, the puzzles and platforming are enjoyable, the different chapter mechanics are simple and engaging. Some of the boss fights can be a little frustrating, and sometimes the server has quite rough lag when playing with friends online, though perhaps that's a clientside Internet issue.

 Definitely worth playing, especially with a S/O. Try not to be impatient if you're way better at platforming than them lol

Bought this to strengthen our friendship.

Instead, it tested our patience, communication skills, and ability to do a single jump.

The story was actually really good... until THE ELEPHANT. Whoever approved that part deserves a raise and a therapist. I went from "Haha, cute co-op game!" to becoming the main villain of the entire gaming industry. I have committed crimes that cannot be forgiven.

The gameplay is absolute peak co-op. Every level throws new mechanics at you, so it never gets boring. The puzzles are fun, and the platforming is great... unless your partner has the jumping ability of a potato. Hearing "I PRESSED SPACE!" for the 47th time through the microphone while watching them miss the easiest jump known to mankind somehow made the game even more enjoyable.

Pro tip: Make sure both of you have decent internet. If one person's connection starts acting up, congratulations—you've both unlocked the hidden difficulty mode called PowerPoint Presentation.

Overall, 10/10.

✔ Lost faith in humanity during the Elephant Arc.
✔ Laughed until my stomach hurt listening to my partner fail parkour.
✔ Friendship somehow survived.
✔ Would absolutely emotionally traumatize an elephant again.

Highly recommended... just don't ask me about the elephant.

Super fun game that stands out in the two player space, especially for couples. 

Connection can be a problem, and the load times are definitely frustrating, but there are rarely any technical issues once you are inside the game. I'm playing on a much older laptop than my wife and was not lagging much throughout two play throughs.

The platforming responds well and I feel the game has enough combination of challenge and ease to appeal to a lot of people of varied experience with games.

Gameplay was a lot of fun and each area is full of creativity, it went in a lot of different directions (fantasy, sci-fi, world in a bottle) that were each developed to feel unique and interconnected. I would definitely recommend this to any gaming couple.

My only complaint is that for a game about repairing a broken marriage, the playable characters spend so much of the first half of the game criticizing and stone walling each other that the happy ending where they agree to work through their differences makes me wonder if they experienced the same journey we did. At no point are either Cody or May willing to give the other the benefit of the doubt or assume anything they say is a valid point and not a personal attack on their worth as a husband/wife/mom/dad/human being.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features checkpoint and respawn locations that reduce the need to replay large sections upon dying.

citations.review_text:
This game surprised me in the best way. 
I've heard beforehand that it's a fun co-op game to play with someone, and that it's a good game in general. I didn't expect to love this game as much as I did. 
The storyline is amazing, the soundtrack is beautiful, the mini games keep it refreshing, and the constant switching of abilities also keep it interesting and fun. But it's also the little things that I liked about this game, for example your re-spawning points when you die are always on good spots, and never on places where you have to redo a lot of what you did before, this I really enjoyed. 
Would recommend. It's fun, cute, sad and overall an amazing game.

Great for local co-op with your partner. The game is really forgiving with frequent auto-saves and respawn points, which keeps the game moving forward even if you don't have much experience playing 3D games.
